title: BUG: import numpy causes python to crash without any error
body:
### Describe the issue:

Actually I am starting to learn OpenCV, when i imported `cv2`, it caused python to crash, then I investigated the cv2 package and found that cv2 internally imports numpy, which was causing the crash. So on checking the `__init__.py` file of `numpy`, I noticed that the statement on line 189 in, `numpy > __init__.py`
```python
core.getlimits._register_known_types()
```
was causing this strange thing. On exploration of source code, I found out that `core > getlimits.py > class MachArLike > __init__() ` was causing it
```python
self.resolution = self._float_to_float(
     self._float_conv(10) ** (-self.precision))
```
After some hit and try, I have figured out there is just a minor change required in this statement
```python
self.resolution = self._float_to_float(
     self._float_conv(10)[0] ** (-self.precision))
```
Please assign this bug to me, I would love to contribute to numpy community.


### Reproduce the code example:

```python
a = 12
b = 2131
print(a+b)

try:
    import numpy
    print("numpy imported")
except:
    print("didn't imported")
```


### Error message:

```shell
no error message, program just abruptly ends like this

```

This works
```
import sys, numpy; print(numpy.version)
```

So it is some interaction betweeen opencv-python and NumPy. The code you point to `self._float_conv(10)` calls `array([10], self.ftype)`, and so somehow on your machine `array([value], self.ftype) ** (-self.precision))` is segfaulting. When you call `self._float_conv(10)[0]` that is returning the python integer `10` (rather than a NumPy `array`) so `10 ** (-self.precision)` succeeds.

Could you print out `pip list`?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
NumPy has an array class, it is very different from `[10]` which is a list containing an integer. When you do `np.array([10]) ** 3` you call into a [ufunc](https://numpy.org/devdocs/glossary.html#term-ufunc) that is set up to repeatedly apply exponentiation on values in a fast manner. One of the things that "fast manner" does is utilize [hardware acceleration](https://numpy.org/devdocs/reference/simd/index.html) called SIMD. Your machine showed it can use 'SSE3', 'SSSE3', 'SSE41', 'POPCNT', 'SSE42' intrinsics to speed up operations. Perhaps in both the VM issue in #22979 and here, the CPU is claiming it properly supports SIMD intrinsics, but in practice the support is faulty.

Unfortunately, NumPy barely supports 32-bit executables running on 64-bit windows. I am afraid it will be very difficult to figure out what is going wrong with a 32-bit version of Windows7. What hardware are you running on? You may want to try to use a version of NumPy without the SIMD optimizations, I think 1.19 was the last version without them. If `pip install "numpy<1.20" gets you a working version of NumPy, then maybe you can find a version of opencv-python that can work with that.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant3 any idea why NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES is failing?

> Also, could you explain those commands? or just give me some resources where I can learn about those.

OPENBLAS_CORETYPE sets the CPU model used by OpenBLAS. One conjecture is that the core model is not being detected properly (you have not told us what hardware you are using). Haswell is a minimal model.

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS sets the maximum number of threads OpenBLAS will use when delegating work.

NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES will tell NumPy not to use certain CPU features. As I wrote [above](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/23074#issuecomment-1400809136), NumPy will try to use low-level parallel routines. Calling one of these when the CPU does not support it will result in the program crashing.

comments.body:
For posterity: the solution for me was to install `numpy==1.23.5` for Python 3.8 (which I use to support Windows 7).

```
pip install numpy==1.23.5
```

Starting with `1.24.0`, it will crash on an ASUS T-100 (64bit CPU, 32bit Windows 10 OS) with Atom CPU that does not support AVX instructions (Celeron and Pentium supposedly [also affected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Vector_Extensions#CPUs_with_AVX))

Interestingly in newer versions (3.11.4) using the latest available numpy (2.2.6) works.

I hope it's OK to document this little piece of info here, it is the 2nd top search result for "python import numpy crashes" but here we have Python 3.8 while https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/23864 involves 3.9, which I did not test.
